title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
task: Evaluating long-horizon agents on real-world business procedures with intermediate constraint validation
key_results: Claude Opus 5 achieves 64.0% strict success, GPT-6 Sol 61.3%; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses ~70% more tool calls than reference executions
comments: The benchmark's emphasis on execution validity rather than outcome alone is valuable, though the gap between goal attainment and strict success suggests agents still struggle with constraint reasoning.

title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
task: Evaluating embodied intelligence of GPT-6-Astra across robotic manipulation and navigation
key_results: GPT-6-Astra shows strong performance on manipulation and navigation benchmarks; real-world deployment reveals gaps in ICL demonstration collection and execution time constraints
comments: The distinction between embodied competence and practical embodied intelligence is insightful, though the paper relies on proprietary model evaluation without ablation details.

hypotheses.hypothesis: GPT-6-Astra has crossed the threshold of embodied competence
hypotheses.result: Largely true, but practical embodied intelligence still unachieved due to ICL data scarcity and real-world constraints

title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
task: Training vision-language models to actively explore 3D environments via reinforcement learning
key_results: ACT3D achieves 53.2% accuracy (22.0% improvement over Qwen base), surpasses Gemini 3.6 Flash while using 50-70% fewer frames; exploration gains highest on questions requiring extensive navigation (16.3% improvement)
comments: The approach elegantly shows that RL-driven exploration emerges without explicit supervision, though generalization to unseen domains remains modest at 5.9% average improvement.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exploration benefits correlate with question difficulty

task: Evaluating AI agents on open scientific research follow-up paper generation
key_results: None of 135 submissions from nine frontier agents satisfy all domain conditions; 114 fail integrity checks for fabricated claims or contradictory numbers
comments: The benchmark's use of domain scientist-verified criteria is rigorous, but the severity of failure (84.4% integrity failure rate) raises concerns about current agent reliability for research.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frontier agents can produce valid follow-up papers meeting domain-scientist conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spatiotemporal allocation strategies improve reconstruction of dynamic regions

title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
task: Using sparse autoencoders as shared coordinate system for matching heterogeneous symbolic systems
key_results: SAE-IDF outperforms dense baseline on 12/12 tasks (Gemma) and 11/12 tasks (Llama); improvements up to 45 points; interpretable dimension attribution via sparse codes
comments: The sparse code representation with IDF reweighting is theoretically motivated for symbol matching; the interpretability via named concepts is valuable for neuro-symbolic systems.

inputs: symbols from two systems in context

hypotheses.hypothesis: SAE sparse codes enable better symbol matching across heterogeneous systems than dense embeddings
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 45-point improvements with interpretable concept attribution

title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription
task: Piano performance-to-score transcription via dual note-frame encoding with temporal positioning
key_results: DuET reduces MUSTER mean error from 6.56% to 3.64% on Gangqinpu and 11.30% to 11.22% on ASAP; improves score timing and notated duration across genres
comments: The dual-encoder architecture with TimeRoPE and TPRoPE effectively models performance-time reference and pitch relationships; cross-attention coupling is well-motivated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual note-frame encoding with shared time reference improves PM2S transcription
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 3.64% MUSTER error (from 6.56%) on Gangqinpu

title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
task: Explicit goal grounding for object-goal navigation using pretrained VLMs
key_results: Explicit grounding achieves SOTA on six benchmarks across three scene collections; with ground-truth grounding, policy nearly matches expert demonstrator, indicating headroom in perception
comments: The diagnosis of goal grounding as dominant failure is insightful; the finding that ground-truth grounding closes the expert gap suggests perception rather than policy is the bottleneck.

model_io.model: VLM-based navigation policy with explicit goal grounding

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit goal grounding improves object-goal navigation success
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SOTA across six benchmarks; closes expert gap with ground-truth grounding

title: Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
task: Discover and characterize small-molecule direct agonists of RIG-I immune receptor
key_results: HTS assay identified small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly trigger CARD (caspase activation and recruitment domain) release from autorepressed protein; lead compound induces robust interferon response
comments: Novel pharmacophore for innate immunity targeting; optical CARD-expulsion monitoring is clever but downstream signaling kinetics and cellular potency need in vivo validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Small molecules can directly activate RIG-I by promoting CARD release from autorepressed conformation
hypotheses.result: Lead agonist achieves robust interferon induction, establishing a new pharmacophore class for RIG-I modulation

title: Multiplexed sensor arrays for high-spatiotemporal decoding of complex physiological networks
task: Design multiplexed biomedical sensor arrays for physiological monitoring
key_results: Framework comparing six multiplexing strategies (time, frequency, spatial, optical, code, hybrid) for independent source recovery under resource constraints
comments: A review synthesizing engineering trade-offs rather than novel experimental data; practical for device design but lacks quantitative validation benchmarks.

title: A thermo-responsive collapse system for controlling heterogeneous cell localization, ratio and interaction for three-dimensional solid tumor modeling
task: Control 3D tumor microenvironment assembly to study NK cell cytotoxicity directionality
key_results: Thermal collapse of strata (TheCOS) enables on-demand multi-population cell positioning; dynein inhibition sustains multi-directional granule dispersion in 3D, expanding bystander killing compared to 2D suspensions
comments: Elegant use of smart polymers to overcome spatial control limitations in tumor models, though quantitative cytotoxicity metrics and kill-zone boundaries need further characterization.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynein inhibition-induced granule dispersion can be maintained in 3D solid tumor-like environments
hypotheses.result: Multi-directional NK cell killing confirmed in 3D via TheCOS imaging, with expanded bystander cytotoxicity compared to 2D

title: Dysregulated thymus-ovary axis promotes virtual memory T cell polarization to aggravate PMOS pathology
task: Identify the thymus-ovary axis mechanism linking androgen excess to ovarian inflammation in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
key_results: Androgen signaling in thymic stromal cells drives early thymic involution; CD8+ virtual memory T cells (TVM) preferentially expand and accumulate in ovaries, secreting pro-inflammatory cytokines/CCL5; JAK inhibition restricts TVM differentiation and ameliorates PMOS pathology
comments: Identification of TVM cells as disease effectors is novel and therapeutically actionable, though the contribution of other thymic cell populations and systemic effects remains underexplored.

model_io.model: PMOS patient cohort and androgen-excess mouse models (athymic, Rag1−/−, WT)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Androgen-induced thymic remodeling impairs T cell output, leading to preferential TVM expansion that sustains ovarian inflammation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: athymic and Rag1−/− mice resistant to pathology; CD8+ TVM cells required for disease; JAK inhibition prevents TVM differentiation

title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
task: Determine Miro1's role in mediating skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
key_results: Miro1 accumulates in muscle of obese/T2D patients and mouse models; inadequate AKT-mediated Miro1 phosphorylation at OMM underlies accumulation; muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves insulin sensitivity; exercise training reduces Miro1 and restores insulin sensitivity
comments: Strong clinical and preclinical correlation, but mechanistic link between Miro1 accumulation and insulin resistance at the molecular level (e.g., mitochondrial function, metabolic readout) could be more explicitly quantified.

model_io.model: Human patients (cross-sectional and RCT) and T2D mouse models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Defective insulin-stimulated AKT-Miro1 interaction causes Miro1 accumulation, impairing mitochondrial dynamics and insulin action
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: impaired AKT-Miro1 interaction in T2D; Miro1 deletion restores sensitivity; exercise relieves accumulation

title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
task: Determine how mechanical strain from phagosomes regulates macrophage phagocytic capacity
key_results: Phagosomes indent the nucleus and increase Lamin B levels; silencing Lamin B or LINC complex components reduced apoptotic body engulfment by ~40-50% in vivo
comments: Novel mechanotransduction mechanism linking nuclear mechanics to immune function, though the quantitative impact on phagocytic capacity in physiological contexts remains to be fully characterized.

inputs: genetic manipulations (Lamin B, LINC complex knockdown)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phagosome-induced nuclear strain triggers LINC/Lamin B-dependent signaling to sustain phagocytic capacity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: LINC and Lamin B silencing suppressed engulfment

title: OSW-1 impairs autophagic flux via AMPK/mTORC1/TFEB-dependent TFEB activation and STX17 downregulation, leading to necroptosis in colorectal cancer
task: Elucidate how OSW-1 induces necroptosis via autophagic flux blockade in colorectal cancer
key_results: OSW-1 activates AMPK/inhibits mTORC1 to promote autophagy initiation, but downregulates STX17 to block autophagosome-lysosome fusion, causing p62 accumulation and RIPK1/RIPK3-mediated necroptosis; tumor growth inhibited in CRC xenografts
comments: Dual-mechanism approach (autophagy initiation + fusion blockade) is mechanistically elegant but the AMPK-independent STX17 downregulation pathway remains incompletely characterized.

model_io.model: CRC cells (in vitro) and CRC xenograft tumors (in vivo)

hypotheses.hypothesis: OSW-1 induces necroptosis by activating autophagy initiation while simultaneously blocking autophagic flux through STX17 downregulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: AMPK/mTORC1/TFEB pathway initiates autophagy; STX17 downregulation blocks fusion; compound C partially rescues flux

title: IκB kinase epsilon deficiency attenuates osteoarthritis-associated pain and synovitis with limited cartilage protection in complementary mouse models
task: Assess IKKε contribution to osteoarthritis structural degeneration, synovitis, and pain
key_results: IKKε deficiency reduced Mmp13 in chondrocytes and Ccl2 in synovial cells; attenuated synovitis and mechanical hypersensitivity in MIA model, but no significant histological cartilage protection in DMM+MCLT model
comments: Selective benefit for pain and inflammation without robust cartilage protection limits clinical translation, and potential compensatory upregulation of IKKβ and TBK1 suggests incomplete mechanistic understanding.

model_io.model: IKKε-deficient mice (in vitro and in vivo)

hypotheses.hypothesis: IKKε promotes OA pathology through c-Jun-dependent catabolic signaling
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed: c-Jun phosphorylation reduced, but p65 phosphorylation unchanged

title: Metaplastic breast carcinoma: a rare breast cancer with distinct biology and therapeutic challenges
task: Characterization of distinct biology and therapeutic targets in metaplastic breast carcinoma
key_results: MpBC exhibits distinct biology from triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, complicating biomarker interpretation and requiring disease-specific therapeutic development
comments: Important clinical recognition of MpBC heterogeneity, but limited to literature review without new experimental data or therapeutic outcomes.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MpBC represents a biologically distinct entity from non-metaplastic TNBC requiring dedicated clinical investigation
hypotheses.result: Supported by literature review of histopathology and differential biology

title: Establishing Polycomb regulatory landscapes in human early development
task: Elucidating H2Aub-dependent establishment of Polycomb repression in human preimplantation development
key_results: H2Aub emerges at two-cell stage in GC-rich regions, progressively accumulates, and drives H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets in blastocysts; H2Aub loss abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment causing moderate gene derepression and impaired development; H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain H3K27me3 in embryonic stem cells
comments: Novel mechanistic insight into Polycomb establishment during human embryogenesis with functional validation via H2Aub loss, though direct causality and developmental outcome specificity require further investigation.

model_io.model: Chromatin profiling (H2Aub, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, DNA methylation)

hypotheses.hypothesis: H2Aub deposition precedes and enables H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets during human development
hypotheses.result: H2Aub emerges early and loss abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets

hypotheses.hypothesis: H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain Polycomb-mediated repression
hypotheses.result: Cooperative regulation demonstrated in embryonic stem cells

title: A unified deep learning framework for multi-lesion detection in diabetic retinopathy using fundus images
task: Multi-lesion diabetic retinopathy detection in fundus images using deep learning with adaptive batch scaling
key_results: U-Net with Adaptive Batch Scaling achieved accuracy 0.925, Dice score 0.771, IoU 0.748, mAP 0.647 on DDR/IDRiD datasets; outperformed Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, Faster R-CNN; simultaneous detection of four lesion types
comments: Well-validated multi-architecture comparison with cross-dataset generalization testing, though clinical deployment metrics (sensitivity/specificity at clinical thresholds) not reported.

model_io.model: Baseline architectures (Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, Faster R-CNN)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive batch scaling optimization improves pixel-level segmentation accuracy for DR lesions
hypotheses.result: U-Net with ABS achieved superior performance across accuracy, Dice, IoU, and mAP metrics

title: Structure-guided design and dynamic evaluation of VP4-targeting siRNAs against rotavirus A
task: Structure-guided siRNA design targeting rotavirus A VP4 gene with RISC compatibility validation
key_results: Three optimized siRNAs designed; siRNA02 showed most favorable AGO2 binding free energy (-453.62 kJ/mol); siRNA01 demonstrated strongest target mRNA interaction (-60.63 kJ/mol); molecular dynamics showed stable AGO2-siRNA-mRNA complexes with RMSD 0.2-0.5 nm
comments: Rigorous computational design pipeline with multiple validation layers, but in vitro/vivo experimental confirmation is needed before clinical development.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structure-guided design with RISC compatibility assessment predicts efficient siRNA candidates for VP4 silencing
hypotheses.result: Two balanced siRNA candidates identified with favorable AGO2 binding and target recognition properties

title: Simultaneous multi-task assessment of five neurological language disorders via cross-corpus multimodal learning
task: Multi-task classification of five neurological language disorders from multimodal spontaneous speech data across corpora
key_results: Test accuracy 90.98%, Macro-F1 86.19% on five disorder classes plus control (1,638 samples); aphasia severity prediction within WAB-AQ measurement error; auxiliary heads enable disease retrieval and longitudinal tracking; Q-Former fusion and class-weighted sampling key drivers
comments: First unified multimodal multi-corpus model for five disorders with impressive accuracy, but zero-shot generalization to unseen classes remains fundamentally limited; MCI-Control confusion suggests need for larger development sets.

model_io.model: Unified multimodal classifier with Q-Former fusion

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal fusion and multi-task learning improve cross-disorder classification compared to single-modality baselines
hypotheses.result: Unified model outperformed all baselines; Q-Former fusion identified as principal performance driver

hypotheses.hypothesis: Paralinguistic features are discriminative across neurological language disorders
hypotheses.result: Inter-disorder correlation analysis identified paralinguistic features among top discriminators

title: A generalizable deep learning model for predicting opioid use disorder using language modeling for cross-EHR data harmonization
task: Opioid use disorder risk prediction from longitudinal EHR data using language model-based feature harmonization
key_results: OUD-REY model: internal AUROC 91.2%, AUPRC 77.0%; external All-of-Us validation AUROC 86.4%, AUPRC 23.1% (2.9% prevalence); VA validation AUROC 85.5%, AUPRC 19.5% (3.5% prevalence); fair across demographics
comments: Strong external validation across two independent health systems with fairness auditing; lower precision in external cohorts reflects baseline OUD prevalence differences, warranting clinical deployment caution.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pretrained language models enable robust feature harmonization across unseen clinical features and health systems
hypotheses.result: External validation maintained high AUROC (85.5-86.4%) despite new dataset and temporal separation

title: Physiologic digital twins for decision support in multi-day ex vivo organ perfusion
task: Organ viability assessment and decision support for ex vivo liver perfusion
key_results: Digital twins integrate mechanistic and statistical models to estimate organ state during multi-day normothermic perfusion, enabling therapeutic window for recovery assessment
comments: Promising approach for transplant optimization, but clinical validation and real-time implementation challenges remain to be demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integration of mechanistic and statistical models improves interpretation of evolving physiologic trajectories without native homeostatic regulation
hypotheses.result: Supported by conceptual framework; experimental validation not provided in abstract

title: A novel cloud-enabled enterprise information systems framework for accelerating digital transformation strategies
task: Cloud-native micro-frontend/microservice co-evolution with drift detection
key_results: 91.4% drift resolution success rate (vs 62.0% rule-based, 71.1% zero-shot LLM, 79.0% partial RL); 80% MTTR reduction, 75% change failure rate reduction, 30pp CPU utilization decrease
comments: Production validation across AWS/GKE/AKS is strong, but the 'drift-aware MDP' formulation and RL+LLM+policy synergy require careful ablation to isolate contributions.

model_io.model: RL agents + LLM synthesizers + policy-as-code governors

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tripartite framework (RL + LLM + policy) yields better drift resolution than any single component
hypotheses.result: Ablation shows complementary contributions; 91.4% vs baselines

title: Data classification and mapping for supporting passenger information systems in railways
task: Data classification and requirement mapping for railway passenger information systems
key_results: Refined data categorization model (accessibility-suitability, demand-supply, dynamic-static spectrum) applied to timetable, occupancy, infrastructure data; data requirement matrix identifies urgent PIS priorities
comments: Conceptual framework is pragmatic but primarily taxonomic; lacks quantitative validation or comparison of outcomes from different data acquisition strategies.

title: Early and reliable short-video news verification through event-aware shot modeling and cross-modal evidence fusion
task: Short-video news verification via event-aware multimodal fusion
key_results: EASE-Fact framework distinguishes inconsistent evidence from unreliable sources; temporal/event-disjoint evaluations support robustness; component ablation validates event-evolution transformer and reliability-aware router
comments: Inspectable diagnostics and source-quality modeling are valuable, but ground-truth factuality remains external; temporal uncertainty is appropriately qualified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit observation boundaries and causal event modeling improve evidence attribution
hypotheses.result: Chronological and event-disjoint evaluations confirm temporal structure importance

title: Application of scanning river surface flow field monitoring system in monitoring complex flow regimes of waterways
task: Non-contact scanning radar monitoring of river surface flow fields
key_results: 120° viewing angle, pulse Doppler with slot antennas and scanning turntables; algorithms (pulse matching, distance-Doppler processing, WSO clustering, ELM networks) stably recover surface and profile velocities in high-noise Yangtze River deployment
comments: Engineering-focused field application with strong anti-interference capability; lacks quantitative error metrics or statistical validation against ground-truth gauges.

model_io.model: Pulse Doppler system + intelligent signal processing
inputs: wide-angle pulse echoes from scanning turntable

title: Analogue fast Fourier transforms for scalable and efficient signal processing
task: Analogue fast Fourier transforms on in-memory computing arrays
key_results: Efficiently mapped FFT algorithm to analogue in-memory systems; demonstrated on up to 65,536-point transforms across 524k charge-trapping memory devices; tested on 1D audio and 2D image signals
comments: Novel hardware-algorithm codesign enabling edge Fourier processing; precision and noise resilience of analogue computation at this scale warrant detailed analysis against digital FFT.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FFT algorithm can be mapped to analogue systems while maintaining scalability without impractical memory arrays
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated 65,536-point transforms on single 524k-device array with precise analogue computations

title: Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system
task: Enabling cavity-controlled superradiant charge density wave ordering in transition-metal dichalcogenides
key_results: Nanoscale grating approach couples cavity photons to electronic density fluctuations with efficiency near Wigner crystallization; threshold pump intensity reduced by matching grating periodicity to enhanced density fluctuations
comments: Proposal uses exciton-polaron processes to bridge optical and electronic length scales, but experimental demonstration remains absent.

model_io.model: Doped TMD coupled to optical cavity with nanoscale grating

hypotheses.hypothesis: Matching grating period to density fluctuations lowers pump threshold
hypotheses.result: Predicted via linear-stability analysis

title: Intrinsic backward emission of coherent Raman photons from homogeneous media
task: Achieving efficient backward coherent Raman scattering from homogeneous media for confocal collection
key_results: Coherent Stokes Raman signals generated into backward hemisphere at levels approaching forward-detected signals; backward collection compatible with fiber coupling and spectrometers
comments: Clever exploitation of wavelength-dependent phase-matching in nonlinear Raman scattering enables practical same-side detection, particularly valuable for opaque samples.

model_io.model: Coherent Stokes Raman scattering in liquids and tissue

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-NA geometries and specific polarizations maximize backward Raman emission
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in simulations and experiments

title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
task: Demonstrating skyrmion Hall-like effect in chiral liquid crystal solitons under shear flow
key_results: Topological solitons (torons, skyrmion tubes) exhibit transverse drift under shear; measured transverse motion much larger than predicted net mass flow and occurs opposite to flow direction
comments: Liquid-crystal analogy cleanly maps to skyrmion Hall physics, though the strong counterintuitive transverse response suggests flow vorticity plays dominant role beyond simple passive-tracer behavior.

model_io.model: Chiral liquid crystal with topological solitons

hypotheses.hypothesis: Solitons undergo transverse motion scaling as shear-rate cubed
hypotheses.result: Weak net mass flow confirmed; soliton motion dominates and opposes predicted direction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Flow vorticity is central to transverse response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via generalized Thiele equation framework

title: Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
task: Identifying spin-fluctuation coupling as primary pairing mechanism in electron-doped cuprates
key_results: Anisotropic inelastic scattering rate correlates with critical temperature; scattering strength from antiferromagnetic fluctuations diminishes with doping and determines Tc in La2−xCexCuO4
comments: Establishes clear electron-boson coupling-Tc link in electron-doped cuprates, but hole-doped materials show different magnetotransport suggesting additional mechanisms beyond spin-fluctuation coupling.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Low-energy spin fluctuations mediate superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by correlation between scattering rate and Tc

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher Tc in hole-doped cuprates arises from stronger spin-fluctuation coupling
hypotheses.result: Rejected—magnetotransport differences suggest alternative mechanisms

title: Pervasive electronic nematicity across the doping-tuned phase diagram of Kagome superconductors
task: Characterizing electronic nematicity in Kagome superconductors independent of charge density waves
key_results: Persistent electronic rotational-symmetry breaking observed across wide doping range in CsV3Sb5; nanoscale nematic domains with three distinct orientations persist after CDW suppression via chemical substitution
comments: Spectroscopic-STM study definitively separates nematic order from CDW, though the microscopic mechanism driving this electronic nematicity remains unresolved.

model_io.model: CsV3Sb5 with Sn/Sb and Ti/V substitutions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Electronic nematicity is independent of 2×2 CDW
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—nematicity persists when CDW is suppressed
